target_customer: AI labs, researchers and regulators who use or cite the ARC-AGI benchmarks; funded by donors and sponsors rather than customers
problem: Existing AI benchmarks saturate and do not measure fluid intelligence, so the field lacks a durable test of progress toward general intelligence.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by donations, with prize money and benchmark evaluations; no revenue model stated

founders.name: Greg Kamradt
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page. Education not listed.

founders.name: Mike Knoop
founders.background_notes: Named on the ARC Prize site; YC page does not profile him.

founders.name: Francois Chollet
founders.background_notes: Creator of ARC-AGI and Keras per the ARC Prize site.

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing benchmarks that resist memorization and brute force is a research problem, and ARC-AGI-3 moved to interactive game environments built by an in-house game studio.

defensibility.rationale: Credibility and adoption by frontier labs make the benchmark a reference point, but benchmarks are open and can be replaced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; labs use the benchmark and have also disputed claims, for example OpenAI questioning an Anthropic ARC-AGI-3 claim per one report.

market_need_then: Frontier labs lacked a benchmark that resisted scaling, and the ARC Prize 2024 competition ran from 2024-06-11 to 2024-11-10 with a pool above 1M, drawing wide participation.

branding.name_origin: ARC refers to the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus benchmark; the site itself does not explain the name beyond the ARC-AGI series.

identity.logo: Brand kit with downloadable logo SVG on the site
identity.visual_style: Grid puzzle visuals from the ARC tasks
identity.voice_and_tone: Research-driven, open source, mission to keep the path to AGI open

branding.brand_signature: The ARC-AGI benchmark series and its public leaderboards
branding.community_and_virality: Large community on Kaggle and in papers; Fast Company coverage, a San Francisco launch event for ARC-AGI-3 on 2026-03-25 with a fireside chat with Sam Altman, and more than 1,200 players of 3,900 games in the preview.

brand_strength.rationale: ARC-AGI is cited by major labs, covered by press and has an active research community, so the name works as an authority signal, though ARC is confusable with other ARC organizations.

pivots.from: ARC Prize as a competition run by Mike Knoop and Francois Chollet
pivots.to: ARC Prize Foundation, a nonprofit benchmark organization
pivots.why: TechCrunch reported in January 2025 that Chollet was co-founding a nonprofit to build AGI benchmarks.

outcome_analysis: The foundation turned a one-off prize into a nonprofit that runs the ARC-AGI benchmark series, with frontier lab adoption, a 2 million dollar 2026 prize on Kaggle and press from launches. Funding sources are not public in what was found, and criticism about overselling the benchmark and disputes over evaluations remain.
notes: Competition list left empty: no dated benchmark competitor near mid 2024 was found in searches. Funding: no donor totals or Form 990 figures found; the Foundation is a nonprofit so no equity rounds. A Digg claim that evaluations of one lab were halted was single-sourced and not recorded. Co-founders Knoop and Chollet are named on the ARC Prize site and YC description, but the YC page lists only Kamradt as a founder profile.
